dedupe_keys.name: klimaateffectatlas climate impact atlas of the netherlands

description: The Klimaateffectatlas is the Netherlands' national atlas of the effects of climate change, with maps for the whole country on pluvial flooding, drought, heat, flooding and water quality, from night-time heat stress to wildfire likelihood and water depth in short intense downpours. Layers are grouped as effects, vulnerability, opportunities for climate adaptation (including green and blue measures), monitoring with several historical moments, area characteristics of landscape, built environment and greenery, and boundaries; many maps have current, 2050 and 2100 versions under low and high KNMI climate scenarios, and a neighbourhood dashboard compares areas. It is coordinated and managed by Climate Adaptation Services for the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, with map content from knowledge institutes and consultancies, and is meant for professionals, for example in climate stress tests. The GIS data are accessible for free download by request form, and the layers are published as WMS services and in an ArcGIS group; data are open under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution 'Klimaateffectatlas, 2026'. Caveats: layers show the best available national public information and are not detailed local models, and downloads need contact details. It supports hazard exposure screening and adaptation planning for infrastructure and green-blue measures; related records are the Copernicus Urban Atlas and Aqueduct flood hazard maps.
